item.title: Trump’s Air Force One Might Get a New Paint Job
item.description: The proposed new livery for Air Force One is darker, with red, white, gold, and navy blue replacing the current sky blue and white pattern. The post Trump’s Air Force One Might Get a New Paint Job appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why Is China Building an Ammunition Plant in Kuwait?
item.description: Though China has sought to make military inroads in the Gulf, the United States remains the region’s unrivaled security partner of choice. The post Why Is China Building an Ammunition Plant in Kuwait? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Last Year’s Boeing Strike Has Delayed F-15EX Deployment to Japan
item.description: The Air Force’s existing F-15 complement at Kadena Air Base in Okinawa is returning to the United States—apparently without anything to replace them. The post Last Year’s Boeing Strike Has Delayed F-15EX Deployment to Japan appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: A Japanese Toilet Maker Could Be the Next Big Thing in AI
item.description: Japanese toilet manufacturer TOTO has extensive experience in ceramics design—processes that could also be used to manufacture the next generation of computer chips. The post A Japanese Toilet Maker Could Be the Next Big Thing in AI appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: As America and Iran Move Toward War, Turkey Is Caught in the Middle
item.description: Few nations in the Middle East have more to lose from a broader US-Iran war than Turkey. The post As America and Iran Move Toward War, Turkey Is Caught in the Middle appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: America’s Unfinished Play in Central Asia
item.description: In Central Asia, Washington must replace episodic symbolism with a sustained economic, legal, and supply-chain strategy. Washington has a habit of chasing symbols when it should be building systems. Greenland is a symbol: icy, strategic, dramatic, and easy to explain in one sentence. Central Asia is a system: less theatrical, more complicated, and vastly more important for […] The post America’s Unfinished Play in Central Asia appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: What Does the Supreme Court’s Tariff Ruling Mean for South Korea?
item.description: The legal basis for a landmark trade deal between South Korea and the Trump administration—lowering tariffs in exchange for investment—now appears in doubt. The post What Does the Supreme Court’s Tariff Ruling Mean for South Korea? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: US Navy Seeks Contractor to Manage New Landing Ships Program
item.description: The US Navy urgently wants to build the Medium Landing Ship on time and on budget—and avoid the issues that forced the early cancellation of the Constellation class. The post US Navy Seeks Contractor to Manage New Landing Ships Program appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The US Air Force Could Finish Restructuring the Sentinel ICBM Program This Year
item.description: The Sentinel nuclear missile was originally scheduled for testing in 2026, but faced significant delays after its skyrocketing budget triggered a rare Nunn-McCurdy breach. The post The US Air Force Could Finish Restructuring the Sentinel ICBM Program This Year appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: How Would a US Strike on Iran Play Out?
item.description: America’s aircraft carriers cannot fight a war on their own, but they can deliver debilitating strikes against adversary nations like Iran. The post How Would a US Strike on Iran Play Out? appeared first on The National Interest.
